editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every card description against its source (ZNE's "zero-noise limit", PEC's "walang kinikilingang pagtatantya" for unbiased estimate, OBP trimming operations "mula sa dulo nito", PNA's absorbing inverses of learned noise channels) and found no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, dropped caveats, or invented claims; register is consistently informal with no po/opo. The defects are surface-level. The SQD card has a real typo that breaks the clause: "gamang magkasama ang quantum at distributed classical computing" — "gamang" is not a word (should be "gamit na magkasama" / "gamit ang quantum at distributed classical computing nang magkasama"). "at the expense of" is calqued literally as "sa gastos ng" in both the PEC and OBP cards (natural Tagalog is "kapalit ng"), "according to the specifics of" becomes the nominalized calque "ayon sa mga partikular ng target na observable" (should be "mga detalye/katangian"), the repeated linkText "Matuto nang higit" is truncated and reads unfinished ("Matuto nang higit pa"), and the AQC-Tensor card has the ungrammatical "ngunit na may mas kaunting layer". One small focus slip: "kapag nagsusumite ng mga job para sa pagpapatupad" is actor-focus with no stated actor, so it can read as if Qiskit Runtime submits the jobs; the English passive "when jobs are submitted" is better served by "kapag isinusumite ang mga job".

examples.source: using quantum and distributed classical computing together
examples.translation: gamang magkasama ang quantum at distributed classical computing
examples.suggested: gamit ang quantum at distributed classical computing nang magkasama
examples.why: "gamang" is not a Tagalog word — an apparent typo for "gamit na", which leaves the clause ungrammatical mid-sentence.

examples.source: at the expense of greater overhead than other techniques such as ZNE / at the cost of more operator measurements
examples.translation: sa gastos ng mas malaking overhead kaysa sa iba pang mga teknik tulad ng ZNE / sa gastos ng mas maraming pagsukat ng operator
examples.suggested: kapalit ng mas malaking overhead ... / kapalit ng mas maraming pagsukat ng operator
examples.why: "sa gastos ng" is a word-for-word calque of "at the expense/cost of"; in Tagalog "gastos" reads as monetary expenditure, and a native technical writer would use "kapalit ng".

examples.source: according to the specifics of the target observable
examples.translation: ayon sa mga partikular ng target na observable
examples.suggested: ayon sa mga detalye ng target na observable
examples.why: "mga partikular" uses the adjective "partikular" as a plural noun, an English-shaped nominalization that does not exist in Tagalog.

examples.source: Learn more
examples.translation: Matuto nang higit
examples.suggested: Matuto nang higit pa
examples.why: "nang higit" without "pa" is a truncated comparative that reads unfinished; repeated six times as the link text.

examples.source: when jobs are submitted for execution
examples.translation: kapag nagsusumite ng mga job para sa pagpapatupad
examples.suggested: kapag isinusumite ang mga job para sa pagpapatupad
examples.why: Actor-focus with no stated actor lets the reader attach the submitting to Qiskit Runtime (the subject of the clause) rather than to the user; the goal-focus form preserves the English passive.

editor_note: The technical content is accurate throughout: the d=1→Z / c=1→X conditions, Bob's CNOT-then-Hadamard order, the B→c and A→d measurement assignment, all four cd cases, and the "(Ang negative-one phase factor ay walang epekto dito.)" caveat all survive intact, and register stays casual with no po/opo. Two wording issues an editor would fix: "complementary aim" is rendered as "layuning kabaligtaran" (= opposite aim), a shift the next sentence luckily repairs, and "so much more difficult ... for the foreseeable future" is flattened to plain "mas mahirap ... sa mahabang panahon", dropping the intensifier that carries the argument. The rest is calque-level: "at the cost of" is literalized as "sa gastos ng" (monetary "expense"; native would be "kapalit ng"), "In words" as bare "Sa salita" instead of "Sa madaling salita", and "is a matter of checking each case" as the English-shaped "ay isang bagay ng pagsusuri ng bawat kaso". Also one aspect slip: "Pagkatapos ay ipadala ni Alice" uses the imperative/infinitive form where "ipinapadala/ipapadala" is needed.

examples.source: Superdense coding is a protocol that, in some sense, achieves a complementary aim to teleportation.
examples.translation: Ang superdense coding ay isang protocol na, sa ilang paraan, ay nakakamit ang layuning kabaligtaran ng teleportation.
examples.suggested: ... ay nakakamit ang layuning komplementaryo sa teleportation.
examples.why: "kabaligtaran" means opposite/contrary, not complementary; the English deliberately says the aims complement each other rather than oppose. The following sentence spells out the actual trade-off, so a learner is not left with a false belief, but the framing word is wrong.

examples.source: Sending qubits is likely to be so much more difficult than sending classical bits for the foreseeable future that trading one qubit ... hardly seems worth it.
examples.translation: Ang pagpapadala ng mga qubit ay malamang na magiging mas mahirap kaysa sa pagpapadala ng mga classical bits sa mahabang panahon kaya ang pag-trade ... ay mukhang hindi masyadong sulit.
examples.suggested: ... ay malamang na magiging napakahirap pa rin — mas mahirap kaysa sa pagpapadala ng mga classical bits — sa nakikinitang hinaharap, kaya ang pagpapalit ...
examples.why: "so much more difficult" is softened to a plain comparative "mas mahirap", weakening the "so ... that" reasoning that makes the trade look unattractive; "foreseeable future" also becomes the vaguer "sa mahabang panahon".

examples.source: at the cost of one e-bit of entanglement
examples.translation: sa gastos ng isang e-bit ng entanglement
examples.suggested: kapalit ng isang e-bit ng entanglement
examples.why: "gastos" is monetary expense; a Tagalog technical writer describing a resource traded away would write "kapalit ng". The calque repeats three times in the file.

examples.source: To verify that the protocol works correctly is a matter of checking each case:
examples.translation: Ang pag-verify na gumagana nang tama ang protocol ay isang bagay ng pagsusuri ng bawat kaso:
examples.suggested: Para mapatunayang gumagana nang tama ang protocol, sapat nang suriin ang bawat kaso:
examples.why: "isang bagay ng pagsusuri" is a word-for-word calque of "a matter of checking" and reads as machine-shaped English syntax in Tagalog.

examples.source: Alice then sends her qubit A to Bob.
examples.translation: Pagkatapos ay ipadala ni Alice ang kanyang qubit $\mathsf{A}$ kay Bob.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos ay ipinapadala ni Alice ang kanyang qubit $\mathsf{A}$ kay Bob.
examples.why: "ipadala" is the infinitive/imperative form, so the sentence reads like an instruction ("then let Alice send") instead of a description of what happens, breaking aspect agreement with the surrounding "nagsasagawa" / "susukatin" narration.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats, or hallucinations; the Hermitian caveat ("Kung ang $O$ ay hindi Hermitian... ang coefficient na $\alpha_k$ ay magiging complex"), the diagonal-basis restriction, and the per-qubit X/Y/Z basis example all track the English exactly, and core terms (observable, qubit, basis, gate, expectation value, Hamiltonian) are kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would change is verb choice and phrasing: "We expand the observable $O$ as" becomes "Inaayos natin ang observable na $O$" ("we arrange/tidy up"), which loses the sense of a basis expansion (the equation still rescues it, so it does not mislead); "could be constructed" becomes "maaaring itayo" (itayo = erect a physical structure, where "mabuo"/"buuin" is the idiomatic choice); "leaves the rest unchanged" is calqued into "iniiwanan ang natitirang hindi nagbabago", which a Tagalog writer would phrase "iniiwang hindi nagbabago ang iba"; and "maaari tayong interesado sa pagsukat" is ungrammatical word order for "maaaring interesado tayo". Also, the "therefore" in "Measuring arbitrary Pauli terms therefore requires a change of basis" is dropped, weakening the causal link to the preceding sentence. None of these is FAIL-level — they are stiffness and imprecise verbs, not false teaching.

examples.source: We expand the observable $O$ as
examples.translation: Inaayos natin ang observable na $O$ bilang
examples.suggested: Ipinapahayag/pinapalawak natin ang observable na $O$ bilang
examples.why: "Inaayos" means "we arrange/fix up"; the point is a basis expansion over all n-qubit Pauli terms, not rearranging. The following equation keeps the learner on track, so it is imprecise rather than misleading.

examples.source: $X_i$ applies an $X$ operator on qubit $i$ and leaves the rest unchanged
examples.translation: ang $X_i$ ay nag-aaplay ng $X$ operator sa qubit $i$ at iniiwanan ang natitirang hindi nagbabago
examples.suggested: ...at iniiwang hindi nagbabago ang iba pang qubit
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English clause order; "iniiwanan ang natitirang hindi nagbabago" reads as machine output — a native writer puts the state before the object.

examples.source: Alternatively, we could be interested in measuring system properties like the average magnetization
examples.translation: Bilang alternatibo, maaari tayong interesado sa pagsukat ng mga katangian ng sistema tulad ng average magnetization
examples.suggested: Bilang alternatibo, maaaring interesado tayong sukatin ang mga katangian ng sistema tulad ng average magnetization
examples.why: "maaari tayong interesado" misplaces the linker; the modal needs "maaaring interesado tayo". Grammatically off in a way no native technical writer would produce.

examples.source: Measuring arbitrary Pauli terms therefore requires a change of basis to diagonalize them.
examples.translation: Ang pagsukat ng mga arbitrary na Pauli term ay nangangailangan ng pagbabago ng basis para i-diagonalize ang mga ito.
examples.suggested: Kaya nangangailangan ng pagbabago ng basis ang pagsukat ng mga arbitrary na Pauli term...
examples.why: The "therefore" that ties this to the preceding diagonal-only-measurement constraint is dropped, so the pedagogical causal chain is stated as an isolated fact. Meaning is still correct — a dropped connective, not a dropped caveat.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, or hallucinated claims; the quantum-utility vs quantum-advantage distinction, the "around 100 qubits" threshold, the wind-tunnel analogy, and the size/quality/speed metric list (including "2-qubit gates are the larger concern") all survive intact, and the emulate-vs-simulate contrast is even preserved as a deliberate "tularan" vs "i-simulate" split. What a native editor would fix is prose quality and a few small word choices: "the prediction of eclipses and tides" becomes "hula ng mga eklipso at alon" (waves, not tides); "Rolf Launduer ... recognized decades ago" becomes "Si Rolf Landauer ... ay nakilala noong matagal na panahon" (passive "was known", losing the attribution of the insight and the "decades"); "essentially pulling physics and computational technology up by the bootstraps" flattens to "mahalagang hinihila ... pataas", where "essentially" was misread as "essential" and the bootstraps image is gone. Two sentences are outright garbled MT artifacts that a reader must re-parse — "Isang beses na kilala si T.J. Watson na hinulaan ang world market" and "hindi kasinit ng prone sa mga error" — plus calques like "Sa paligid ng 100 qubit", "maraming-facet na koneksyon", "ito ay dalawang-daan", "ngunit kung at saan lamang", and "paganahin kang gawin ito" for "enable you to do this". Informal register holds (no po/opo); none of these would teach a learner a false concept.

examples.source: Historical uses in this category have included the prediction of eclipses and tides
examples.translation: Ang mga makasaysayang gamit sa kategoryang ito ay kinabibilangan ng hula ng mga eklipso at alon
examples.suggested: ... hula ng mga eklipse at ng pagtaas-pagbaba ng tubig (tides)
examples.why: "alon" means waves, not tides. Tide-prediction machines are the actual historical computing example being cited, so the illustration loses its referent.

examples.source: T.J. Watson once famously predicted a world market for just a few computers.
examples.translation: Isang beses na kilala si T.J. Watson na hinulaan ang world market para sa ilang computer lamang.
examples.suggested: Sikat ang hula ni T.J. Watson noon na iilang computer lang ang kakailanganin ng buong mundo.
examples.why: "Isang beses na kilala si..." is a word-for-word rendering of "once famously" that produces broken Tagalog; the reader has to reconstruct the sentence. No native writer would open the conclusion this way.

examples.source: Gates that run on single qubits are not as prone to errors as 2-qubit gates
examples.translation: Ang mga gate na tumatakbo sa mga solong qubit ay hindi kasinit ng prone sa mga error tulad ng mga 2-qubit gate
examples.suggested: Ang mga gate na tumatakbo sa iisang qubit ay hindi kasing-dali magkamali ng mga 2-qubit gate
examples.why: "kasinit" is not a word (a mangled "kasing-"), and "kasing... tulad ng" doubles the comparative. The direction of the comparison is still recoverable, so it misfires on fluency rather than meaning.

examples.source: essentially pulling physics and computational technology up by the bootstraps
examples.translation: mahalagang hinihila ang physics at computational na teknolohiya pataas
examples.why: "essentially" is mistranslated as "mahalagang" (importantly), and the bootstraps image — each field lifting the other with no outside help — collapses into a plain "pulling upward", so the two-way-street point loses its punchline.

examples.source: Rolf Launduer, a computer scientist (and IBMer), recognized decades ago that information is physical
examples.translation: Si Rolf Landauer, isang computer scientist (at IBMer), ay nakilala noong matagal na panahon na ang impormasyon ay pisikal
examples.suggested: Si Rolf Landauer ... ay kinilala/natukoy ilang dekada na ang nakalipas na pisikal ang impormasyon
examples.why: "nakilala" reads as "was known/became acquainted", flipping the voice so the sentence no longer clearly says Landauer was the one who realized this; "decades ago" is also blurred into a vague "noong matagal na panahon".

examples.source: we're likely to see a back-and-forth interaction with classical computing
examples.translation: malamang na makakita tayo ng magkasalungat na interaksyon sa klasikal na computing
examples.suggested: malamang na makakita tayo ng pabalik-balik na palitan sa klasikal na computing
examples.why: "magkasalungat" means contradictory/opposing rather than alternating back-and-forth. The following sentence spells out the alternating pattern, so the learner recovers it, but the setup word points the wrong way.

examples.source: At around 100 qubits ... enable you to do this ... multifaceted connections
examples.translation: Sa paligid ng 100 qubit ... paganahin kang gawin ito ... maraming-facet na koneksyon
examples.suggested: Sa humigit-kumulang 100 qubit ... bigyan ka ng kakayahang gawin ito ... koneksyon nito sa maraming aspeto
examples.why: Cluster of calques: "sa paligid ng" is the spatial "around", "paganahin" is the machine sense of "enable", and "maraming-facet" is a half-translated compound. Each is understandable but stacks up into a machine-translated texture.

editor_note: Two prose verbs are replaced by words that say something the English does not. In the Overview, "you can solve domain-specific partial differential equations" becomes "maaari kang magsulsi ng domain-specific partial differential equations" — "magsulsi" means to darn/mend cloth, not to solve; the file's own frontmatter uses the correct "naglulutas", so the core capability sentence is both wrong and inconsistent with the page's own description. In the Material deformation section, "the bulk modulus of the material being stretched" becomes "ang bulk modulus ng materyal na inuuntog" — "inuuntog" means being banged/knocked, which directly contradicts the tensile test just described two sentences earlier (a bar pulled at its far end); the same section renders "stretch" correctly as "maunat" in the next paragraph, so the physical setup no longer matches itself. Two smaller drifts: "a bar fixed in space" is rendered "isang bar na nakaayos sa espasyo" ("arranged in space" rather than held immobile), and "trial solutions get gradually closer to the actual solutions" is flattened to "unti-unting humahantong sa mga aktwal na solusyon" ("gradually lead to"), losing the convergence intuition. Everything else — the CFD grid values, the benchmark table, the optimizer-chaining paragraph, the noise-learner/shots explanation — is faithful, and the informal register holds throughout with no po/opo.

examples.source: With the QUICK-PDE function, you can solve domain-specific partial differential equations on IBM Quantum QPUs.
examples.translation: Sa pamamagitan ng QUICK-PDE function, maaari kang magsulsi ng domain-specific partial differential equations sa IBM Quantum QPUs.
examples.suggested: …maaari kang maglutas ng domain-specific partial differential equations sa IBM Quantum QPUs.
examples.why: "Magsulsi" means to darn or mend fabric, not to solve. The single most important capability sentence on the page becomes nonsense, and it contradicts the frontmatter description, which correctly uses "naglulutas".

examples.source: $K$ represents the bulk modulus of the material being stretched
examples.translation: Ang $K$ ay kumakatawan sa bulk modulus ng materyal na inuuntog
examples.suggested: Ang $K$ ay kumakatawan sa bulk modulus ng materyal na iniuunat
examples.why: "Inuuntog" means being banged or knocked. The section has just set up a one-dimensional tensile test where a bar is pulled, and the next paragraph correctly says "maunat ang bar" — so the parameter gloss now describes a different (compressive/impact) experiment than the one being solved.

examples.source: a bar fixed in space is pulled at its other extremity
examples.translation: ang isang bar na nakaayos sa espasyo ay hinihila sa kabilang dulo nito
examples.suggested: ang isang bar na nakapirmi sa espasyo ay hinihila sa kabilang dulo nito
examples.why: "Nakaayos" means arranged or organized, not clamped/held immobile. The boundary condition that one end is fixed is the whole point of the tensile-test setup, and that constraint is lost.

examples.source: The trial solutions get gradually closer to the actual solutions until you reach a satisfactory result.
examples.translation: Ang mga trial solution ay unti-unting humahantong sa mga aktwal na solusyon hanggang sa makamit mo ang kasiya-siyang resulta.
examples.suggested: Ang mga trial solution ay unti-unting lumalapit sa mga aktwal na solusyon hanggang sa makamit mo ang kasiya-siyang resulta.
examples.why: "Humahantong sa" means "lead to" — it implies arrival, not asymptotic approach. The convergence intuition that makes the hybrid optimization loop understandable is flattened.

editor_note: The physics and math survive intact: every win/lose condition, the (1,1) inversion ("mananalo sina Alice at Bob kapag ang a at b ay *magkaiba*"), the 3/4 classical bound, the (2+√2)/4 ≈ 0.85 quantum value and Tsirelson's optimality claim are all faithful, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still change: the intro promises "kung ano ang nagpapagana nito" (what makes it *work*) where the English says "what makes it interesting"; "instance of a nonlocal game" is rendered "pagkakataon" (occasion/opportunity), the wrong sense of "instance"; the "each" is dropped from "Alice and Bob can each choose from four possible functions," so the jump to 16 strategies loses its arithmetic justification; and "anggulo na" is fused into the non-word "anggulona" in seven places (lines 192, 574, 580, 591, 597, 625, 631), alongside the typos "pag-alabalahin" (for pag-aalalahanin), "nangyara" (nangyari) and "patatalo". None of these teach a false concept, but several sentences read as unedited MT — "sa bawat oras" for "every time", "sa paligid ng pinagmulan" for "about the origin", "Nananatiling malaman kung gaano kahusay...".

examples.source: we'll focus in on the CHSH game and what makes it interesting
examples.translation: itutuon natin ang ating pansin sa CHSH na laro at kung ano ang nagpapagana nito
examples.suggested: ...at kung bakit ito kawili-wili
examples.why: "nagpapagana" means "makes it function/run"; the lesson's framing promise (why the game is interesting) is replaced by a claim about how it operates.

examples.source: Alice and Bob can each choose from four possible functions from one bit to one bit ... so there are 16 different deterministic strategies in total
examples.translation: Maaaring pumili sina Alice at Bob mula sa apat na posibleng function mula sa isang bit patungo sa isang bit ... kaya mayroon 16 na iba't ibang deterministikong estratehiya sa kabuuan
examples.suggested: Maaaring pumili ang bawat isa kina Alice at Bob mula sa apat na posibleng function ...
examples.why: The load-bearing "each" is gone, so 4 x 4 = 16 no longer follows from the sentence; the count is asserted without its reason.

examples.source: A precise description of the referee defines an instance of a nonlocal game.
examples.translation: Ang tumpak na paglalarawan ng tagahatol ay tumutukoy ng isang pagkakataon ng isang nonlocal na laro.
examples.suggested: ...ay tumutukoy sa isang tiyak na instansya ng isang nonlocal na laro.
examples.why: "pagkakataon" is "occasion/opportunity", not "instance" in the problem-specification sense used here.

examples.source: for each angle theta / the cosine-squared of this angle
examples.translation: para sa bawat anggulona $\theta$ / ang cosine-squared ng anggulona ito
examples.suggested: para sa bawat anggulong $\theta$ / ang cosine-squared ng anggulong ito
examples.why: "anggulona" is a non-word from a fused "anggulo na"; it repeats seven times, blanketing the geometric-picture section.

examples.source: No deterministic strategy can possibly win the CHSH game every time. / it rotates ... about the origin / It remains to figure out how well this strategy works.
examples.translation: Walang deterministikong estratehiya ang maaaring manalo ... sa bawat oras. / inog-ikot nito ang mga vector ... sa paligid ng pinagmulan / Nananatiling malaman kung gaano kahusay ang estratehiyang ito
examples.suggested: ...manalo sa tuwina / ...pinaiikot ang mga vector sa paligid ng origin / Ang natitira na lang ay alamin kung gaano kahusay ...
examples.why: Word-for-word calques: "sa bawat oras" reads as "every hour", "pinagmulan" is origin-as-source rather than the geometric origin, and "Nananatiling malaman" is a construction no Tagalog technical writer would produce.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the delicate Pauli-twirling paragraph survives intact (left/right Paulis cancelling around the two-qubit gate, "ginagawa nitong stochastic errors ang mga coherent errors", the analysis-pass "hindi nila mababago ang DAG, ngunit maaari nilang baguhin ang property_set" contrast, and "patakbuhin ito sa 50 circuits" all match the English), and register stays casual with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would change is smaller: "directed edges" is rendered "mga direktibong edges" (line 44), where *direktibo* means "directive," not "may direksyon" — and the same concept is later correctly called "mga direksyonal na edges" in the DAG image alt text (line 75), so the file is internally split on a core graph-theory term. Line 80 has a grammatical/calque slip, "Ito ay kakaibang sa mga transformation pass" for "This contrasts with transformation passes" (should be "Kabaligtaran ito ng…" or at minimum "kakaiba sa"). Two smaller word-choice slips: "naranasan" (past) for the habitual "experience" in line 83, and "iba ang paraan ng pagganap ng mga ito" where *pagsasagawa* is the natural rendering of "the way they are performed."

examples.source: a DAG is composed of *vertices* … and directed *edges* that connect pairs of vertices
examples.translation: binubuo ng mga *vertices* … at mga direktibong *edges* na nag-uugnay ng mga pares ng vertices
examples.suggested: … at mga *edges* na may direksyon (o: mga nakadirektang edges) na nag-uugnay …
examples.why: 'direktibo' means 'directive/instructional', not 'directed'. The alt text at line 75 already uses the better 'mga direksyonal na edges', so the same core graph concept is rendered two ways within one file.

examples.source: This contrasts with transformation passes, which do modify the DAG
examples.translation: Ito ay kakaibang sa mga transformation pass, na binabago ang DAG
examples.suggested: Kabaligtaran ito ng mga transformation pass, na binabago ang DAG
examples.why: Ungrammatical linker ('kakaibang sa') and a stiff calque of 'this contrasts with'; a native technical writer would use 'Kabaligtaran nito…' or 'Sa kabilang banda…'.

examples.source: randomizes how qubits experience noisy channels
examples.translation: nagra-randomize ng paraan kung paano naranasan ng mga qubit ang mga maingay na channel
examples.suggested: …kung paano nararanasan ng mga qubit ang mga maingay na channel
examples.why: Perfective 'naranasan' reads as a one-off past event; the English describes an ongoing/general behavior, which Tagalog marks with the imperfective 'nararanasan'.

examples.source: the two-qubit operations are identical, but the way they are performed is different
examples.translation: magkapareho ang mga two-qubit operation, ngunit iba ang paraan ng pagganap ng mga ito
examples.suggested: …ngunit iba ang paraan ng pagsasagawa ng mga ito
examples.why: 'pagganap' reads as 'performance/achievement' (as in how well something performs), not 'how it is carried out'; 'pagsasagawa' is the term a technical writer would use here.

editor_note: Two meaning errors in the last 40% of the file. (1) In the PEA paragraph, "This isn't available in Qiskit yet, but it will be later this year" becomes "ngunit ito ay magagamit sa susunod na taon" — "next year," a different availability timeline than the source states. (2) In the PEC paragraph, "modify your circuits so that they effectively have the opposite Pauli gates built in" becomes "para epektibo nilang itago ang kabaligtarang mga Pauli gate" — "itago" means "hide/conceal," so the sentence describes PEC as hiding the inverse Pauli gates rather than building them into the circuit, garbling the mechanism the paragraph is teaching. Secondary, non-misleading issues: the existential "Mayroon" is repeatedly used without its linker ("Mayroon apat na antas," "Mayroon dalawang primitive," "Mayroon maraming teknik" — should be "Mayroong"); English discourse adverbs are left untranslated mid-sentence ("Essentially, sinasangkot nito…", "ay essentially ay nagtatanong" with a doubled "ay", "Specifically, kinakalkula nito…"); "noise" is kept in English everywhere except one slip to "ingay" in the transpiler section; and "measurements" in the circuit definition is rendered "sukatan" (metric — the word already used for the EPLG/CLOPS performance metrics) while the very next paragraph correctly uses "pagsukat".

examples.source: This isn't available in Qiskit yet, but it will be later this year.
examples.translation: Hindi ito available sa Qiskit pa, ngunit ito ay magagamit sa susunod na taon.
examples.suggested: Hindi pa ito available sa Qiskit, ngunit magiging available ito bago matapos ang taon.
examples.why: "sa susunod na taon" = next year; the source says later this year. The reader is given a different availability timeline than the English asserts.

examples.source: you can modify your circuits so that they effectively have the opposite Pauli gates built in to cancel these noise channels
examples.translation: maaari mong baguhin ang iyong mga circuit para epektibo nilang itago ang kabaligtarang mga Pauli gate para kanselahin ang mga noise channel na ito
examples.suggested: maaari mong baguhin ang iyong mga circuit para epektibong nakapaloob na rito ang kabaligtarang mga Pauli gate na kakansela sa mga noise channel na ito
examples.why: "itago" means hide/conceal, not "have built in". The sentence now describes PEC as hiding gates instead of inserting inverse Pauli gates into the circuit — the core mechanism of the technique is misdescribed.

examples.source: There are four optimization levels… / There are two primitives to choose from… / There are multiple techniques…
examples.translation: Mayroon apat na antas ng optimization… / Mayroon dalawang primitive na mapagpipilian… / Mayroon maraming teknik…
examples.suggested: Mayroong apat na antas… / Mayroong dalawang primitive… / Mayroong maraming teknik…
examples.why: Existential "mayroon" requires the linker -ng before the counted noun; the bare form repeated three times reads as machine output, not as a native technical writer.

examples.source: optimize the circuit for execution and resilience against noise
examples.translation: i-optimize ang circuit para sa execution at katatagan laban sa ingay
examples.suggested: …katatagan laban sa noise
examples.why: "noise" is kept in English consistently throughout the error-suppression and mitigation sections; this lone "ingay" (everyday sound) breaks the file's own convention for the domain term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful end to end — no drift, no dropped caveats, no invented claims; the batch section and the six Next-steps bullets match the English one for one, and register stays informal. Two editorial slips: "measurement outcome" is rendered "resulta ng sukat" in both section blurbs (lines 36 and 80), where "sukat" is the noun for size/measure — a Tagalog quantum writer would say "resulta ng pagsukat" for the act of measurement; it is recognizable, not false. Also, in the lede (line 32) "search and classification algorithms" becomes "mga algorithm ng paghahanap at pag-classify", which mixes a Tagalog nominalization with an untranslated English verb stem; "klasipikasyon" would parallel "paghahanap" cleanly. Minor also: "working through the Cost function lesson" → "paggawa ng" (literally "making"), where "pagdaan sa" or "pag-aaral ng" is the idiomatic reading.

examples.source: Use Sampler to return the measurement outcome as bitstrings or counts of a single circuit.
examples.translation: Gamitin ang Sampler para ibalik ang resulta ng sukat bilang mga bitstring o count ng isang circuit.
examples.suggested: Gamitin ang Sampler para ibalik ang resulta ng pagsukat bilang mga bitstring o count ng isang circuit.
examples.why: "sukat" is the noun for size/measure; the quantum-measurement sense needs the gerund "pagsukat". Used the same way in both blurbs, so it is consistent but consistently off.

examples.source: Leverage Sampler's capabilities for search and classification algorithms like Grover's and QVSM.
examples.translation: Gamitin ang mga kakayahan ng Sampler para sa mga algorithm ng paghahanap at pag-classify tulad ng Grover's at QVSM.
examples.suggested: ...para sa mga algorithm ng paghahanap at klasipikasyon tulad ng Grover's at QVSM.
examples.why: "pag-classify" pairs a Tagalog prefix with a bare English verb stem next to the fully Tagalog "paghahanap"; the coordination reads unbalanced to a native technical writer.

examples.source: Practice with primitives by working through the Cost function lesson in IBM Quantum Learning.
examples.translation: Magsanay sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng [Cost function lesson] sa IBM Quantum Learning.
examples.suggested: Magsanay sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng pagdaan sa [Cost function lesson] sa IBM Quantum Learning.
examples.why: "paggawa ng" means "making/creating" the lesson rather than working through an existing one — a literal calque of "working through".

editor_note: Two genuinely misleading errors. (1) Line 68 inverts the commutation condition: "act nontrivially on disjoint sets of qubits" is rendered "kumikilos sila nang nontrivially sa magkaparehong mga qubit" (= on the SAME qubits), which is the exact opposite and directly contradicts the very next sentence ("Ang natitirang posibilidad ay ... magkapatong"), so the learner is taught that overlapping generators are the trivially-commuting case. (2) Line 87 renders "at least one quantum state vector is FIXED by all the stabilizer generators" as "ay naayos ng lahat ng stabilizer generator" — "naayos" means repaired/corrected (the same word the file uses for error correction in line 168), not left invariant, so the third stabilizer condition is taught wrong. Also dropped: the English clarifying caveat defining "horizontal/vertical lattice line" as a full row/column (not the loop's segments) and the "since each lattice line crosses the closed loop ... once in, once back out" justification are both missing from the Tagalog list intro (lines 143-145). Secondary: line 132 is garbled ("ay hindi kaya nde-detect ng code"), line 109 uses the non-word "malintuindihan" for "This is intuitive", line 153 calls a *loop* a "chain" ("Ang ganitong chain ng mga error"), collapsing the chain/loop distinction the section is built on, and "measurement" is consistently rendered as the noun "sukat" (size) rather than "pagsukat".

examples.source: The $Z$ and $X$ stabilizer generators clearly commute when they act nontrivially on disjoint sets of qubits, like for the examples shown in the previous figure.
examples.translation: Ang mga $Z$ at $X$ stabilizer generator ay malinaw na nagko-commute kapag kumikilos sila nang nontrivially sa magkaparehong mga qubit, tulad ng sa mga halimbawa sa nakaraang figure.
examples.suggested: ... kapag kumikilos sila nang nontrivially sa magkahiwalay (disjoint) na mga set ng qubit, ...
examples.why: Inverted condition: 'disjoint' became 'magkapareho' (the same). It teaches the opposite rule and contradicts the following sentence, which introduces overlap as the REMAINING case.

examples.source: The final condition required of stabilizer generators is that at least one quantum state vector is fixed by all of the stabilizer generators.
examples.translation: Ang huling kinakailangang kondisyon ng mga stabilizer generator ay ang kahit isang quantum state vector ay naayos ng lahat ng stabilizer generator.
examples.suggested: ... ay may kahit isang quantum state vector na hindi nababago (nananatiling pareho / fixed) ng lahat ng stabilizer generator.
examples.why: 'Fixed' here means left invariant, not repaired. 'Naayos' is the same verb the file uses for correcting errors (line 168), so the learner reads the condition as being about error correction.

examples.source: Here, a 'horizontal/vertical lattice line' means a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error). ... The example shown above falls into this category, since each lattice line crosses the closed loop of errors once, say crossing into the closed loop, and once crossing back out of the closed loop of errors.
examples.translation: Sa partikular, maaaring ilarawan ang iba't ibang uri ng loop tulad ng sumusunod. ... (Ang halimbawa na ipinakita sa itaas ay nahuhulog sa kategoryang ito.)
examples.suggested: Add the definition of 'pahalang/patayong linya ng lattice' as a full row/column of qubits, and restore the 'dahil bawat linya ng lattice ay tumatawid sa closed loop nang isang beses papasok at isang beses palabas' justification.
examples.why: A definitional caveat and the reasoning that makes category 1 comprehensible are both dropped; the Tagalog states the classification without the explanation the English gives.

examples.source: Such a loop of $X$ errors is not contained in the stabilizer because every $X$ stabilizer generator places an even number of $X$ operations on each horizontal lattice line...
examples.translation: Ang ganitong chain ng mga error ay hindi nasa stabilizer dahil ang bawat $X$ stabilizer generator ay naglalagay ng pantay na bilang ng mga $X$ operation sa bawat pahalang na linya...
examples.suggested: Ang ganitong loop ng mga $X$ error ay hindi nasa stabilizer ...
examples.why: The section hinges on chain (has endpoints, detected) vs loop (no endpoints, may be undetected). Calling this loop a 'chain' blurs exactly that distinction.

examples.source: This is intuitive when we consider $Z$ stabilizer generators... / Closed loops of adjacent $X$ errors are therefore not detected by the code.
examples.translation: Ito ay malintuindihan kapag isinaalang-alang natin... / Ang mga closed loop ng magkakatabi na $X$ error ay hindi kaya nde-detect ng code.
examples.suggested: Madaling maintindihan ito kapag... / Kaya hindi nade-detect ng code ang mga closed loop ng magkakatabi na $X$ error.
examples.why: 'Malintuindihan' is not a Tagalog word, and 'hindi kaya nde-detect' is garbled (stray 'kaya' plus a misspelled 'nade-detect').

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the three modes (job/session/batch), the Open Plan restriction ("hindi makakapag-submit ng mga session job"), the close-session advice, and the PUB parameter note all match the English, and the informal register holds throughout with no po/opo. Three small editorial slips remain. First, the emphasis marker "particularly" is dropped in line 43 — "which can be particularly useful for iterative tasks" becomes a flat "na maaaring maging kapaki-pakinabang", losing the English's pointed recommendation. Second, "Mag-practis sa mga primitive" (line 275) uses a nonstandard Taglish respelling no Tagalog technical writer would publish; "Magsanay" (or plain "mag-practice") is the natural form. Third, "isang solong parameter" (line 144) is a calque of "a single parameter" — idiomatic Tagalog is "iisang parameter". All are style/qualifier-level, not meaning-level.

examples.source: which can be particularly useful for iterative tasks that require frequent communication between classical and quantum resources
examples.translation: na maaaring maging kapaki-pakinabang para sa mga iterative na gawain na nangangailangan ng madalas na komunikasyon sa pagitan ng mga classical at quantum na mapagkukunan
examples.suggested: na partikular na kapaki-pakinabang para sa mga iterative na gawain na nangangailangan ng madalas na komunikasyon sa pagitan ng classical at quantum na mapagkukunan
examples.why: 'particularly' is dropped and 'can be' added, flattening a targeted recommendation into a generic 'maaaring ... kapaki-pakinabang'. Pedagogically the reader loses the cue that sessions are especially suited to this case.

examples.source: Practice with primitives by working through the Cost function lesson
examples.translation: Mag-practis sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng pagtatapos ng aralin sa Cost function
examples.suggested: Magsanay sa mga primitive sa pamamagitan ng pagdaan sa aralin sa Cost function
examples.why: 'Mag-practis' is a nonstandard phonetic respelling of the English verb; standard Tagalog technical prose uses 'Magsanay' (or keeps 'mag-practice' intact). 'pagtatapos' also reads as 'finishing' rather than 'working through'.

examples.source: can either be a single parameter or a list of parameters
examples.translation: ay maaaring isang solong parameter o isang listahan ng mga parameter
examples.suggested: ay maaaring iisang parameter o isang listahan ng mga parameter
examples.why: 'solong' is a literal rendering of 'single' that reads as 'solo/alone'; 'iisang' is the idiomatic Tagalog quantifier here and avoids the calqued feel.

editor_note: Three meaning-level defects push this past MINOR. (1) The *salt* tooltip (line 528) inverts the security claim: English says salt makes a password "unique, distinctive, and hard to reproduce", but the Tagalog ends "...at nagpapadali ng reproduksyon nito" — "and makes it EASY to reproduce", teaching the opposite of why salting exists. (2) In the elliptic-curve addition definition (line 1467) "intersect" is rendered four times as "tumutugma" (matches/corresponds) instead of "tumatawid/humahalang", and "the point opposite R reflected through the x-axis" becomes "na nairerepresenta sa pamamagitan ng x-axis" (represented through the x-axis) — the central geometric construction of P+Q = −R no longer describes a line crossing the curve or a reflection; note line 1452 uses the correct "magtatawid", so the file is also self-inconsistent. (3) In Shor's algorithm step 3 (line 748) "If r is odd" becomes "Kung ang r ay kakaiba" ("if r is strange/unusual"), an unusable branch condition beside the correct "pantay" for even. Lesser slips: "intercept" → "mapigilan" (block/prevent) at line 419 where "humarang" is used correctly at lines 933/994; the heading "Simulating a Key Encapsulation Mechanism" → "Pagsimula ng..." (starting) at line 466 while the body correctly says "gayahin"; and "intractable / computationally infeasible" hardened to "hindi malulutas" (unsolvable) at lines 1483/1504. Register is correctly casual throughout and the RSA/DSA/DH prose is otherwise faithful and readable.

examples.source: ...makes our password unique, distinctive, and hard to reproduce.
examples.translation: ...nagpapanatatangi ng ating password, nagpapaiba nito, at nagpapadali ng reproduksyon nito.
examples.suggested: ...ginagawang natatangi ang ating password, nagpapaiba nito, at nagpapahirap na maulit o ma-reproduce ito.
examples.why: Direct inversion: 'hard to reproduce' becomes 'makes it easy to reproduce'. A learner is taught that salting makes a hashed password EASIER to recreate — the opposite of the security property being explained. Also 'nagpapanatatangi' is a malformed word.

examples.source: Draw the line that intersects P and Q and find the third point, R, at which the line intersects the curve again. We then define P + Q = −R, the point opposite R reflected through the x-axis... When the line through P, Q does not intersect the curve at any finite (x, y)...
examples.translation: Iguhit ang linya na tumutugma sa $P$ at $Q$ at hanapin ang ikatlong punto, $R$, kung saan muling tumutugma ang linya sa kurba. Tinutukoy natin ang $P + Q = −R$, ang punto na kabaligtaran ng $R$ na nairerepresenta sa pamamagitan ng $x$-axis... Kapag ang linya sa pamamagitan ng $P, Q$ ay hindi tumutugma sa kurba sa anumang finite na $(x, y)$...
examples.suggested: Iguhit ang linyang dumadaan sa $P$ at $Q$ at hanapin ang ikatlong punto, $R$, kung saan muling tumatawid ang linya sa kurba. Tinutukoy natin na $P + Q = -R$, ang puntong salungat kay $R$ na sinasalamin sa $x$-axis... Kapag ang linyang dumadaan sa $P, Q$ ay hindi tumatawid sa kurba sa anumang finite na $(x, y)$...
examples.why: 'Intersect' is rendered as 'tumutugma' (matches/corresponds) four times, and 'reflected through the x-axis' as 'nairerepresenta' (is represented). The whole mechanism of elliptic-curve point addition — a line crossing the curve, then reflecting the third point — is lost. Line 1452 already uses the correct 'magtatawid', so the file contradicts itself.

examples.source: If r is odd, go back to step 1 and try a different choice for a.
examples.translation: Kung ang $r$ ay kakaiba, bumalik sa hakbang 1 at subukan ang ibang pagpipilian para sa $a$.
examples.suggested: Kung ang $r$ ay gansal (odd), bumalik sa hakbang 1 at subukan ang ibang pagpipilian para sa $a$.
examples.why: 'Odd' (parity) is rendered as 'kakaiba' = strange/unusual. In a numbered algorithm step whose sibling clause correctly uses 'pantay' for even, the learner is given a branch condition that does not state a testable property.

examples.source: Any one can intercept the public key and read off the public numbers (e,n) that form the key.
examples.translation: Maaaring mapigilan ng sinuman ang public key at mabasa ang mga public number $(e,n)$ na bumubuo sa key.
examples.suggested: Maaaring maharang ng sinuman ang public key at mabasa ang mga public number $(e,n)$ na bumubuo sa key.
examples.why: 'Intercept' becomes 'mapigilan' (block/prevent), which reads as 'anyone can stop the public key'. The same verb is correctly rendered 'humarang' at lines 933 and 994, so this is both wrong and inconsistent.

examples.source: ##### Simulating a Key Encapsulation Mechanism with RSA in Python
examples.translation: ##### Pagsimula ng Key Encapsulation Mechanism gamit ang RSA sa Python
examples.suggested: ##### Paggaya sa Key Encapsulation Mechanism gamit ang RSA sa Python
examples.why: 'Simulating' becomes 'Pagsimula' (starting/beginning). The section body correctly says 'para gayahin ang isang KEM', so the heading promises something different from what the section does.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every paragraph tracks the English, including the tricky Step 5 passage (template circuit structurally equivalent, single-qubit gates replaced by parameterized gates, samplex encodes the randomization info) and the "25 shots" / "does not make any implicit decisions … full control and transparency" claims. Register is correctly casual (mo/iyong, no po/opo) and domain terms are kept in English consistently (circuit, gate, shots, twirling, backend, transpile as "i-transpile"). What a native editor would still change is wording, not meaning: "prescribed annotations" is rendered "inireseta na annotation" — "inireseta" reads as a medical prescription in Tagalog and should be "itinakda/nakatakdang annotation"; "Maaari itong may mga opsyonal na parameter" (Step 2) is ungrammatical for "It can optionally have parameters" (natural: "Opsyonal na magkaroon ito ng mga parameter"); "structurally katumbas" leaves the English adverb bare where "katumbas sa istruktura" is idiomatic; and "Karaniwang," in Step 3 should be the sentence adverb "Karaniwan,".

examples.source: in order to implement the prescribed annotations (gate and measurement twirling, in this example)
examples.translation: para ipatupad ang mga inireseta na annotation (gate at measurement twirling, sa halimbawang ito)
examples.suggested: para ipatupad ang mga itinakdang annotation (gate at measurement twirling, sa halimbawang ito)
examples.why: "Inireseta" in Tagalog overwhelmingly means a doctor's prescription; for "prescribed/specified" in a technical sense the natural word is "itinakda" or "nakasaad". Meaning is still recoverable, so this is a word-choice slip, not drift.

examples.source: It can optionally have parameters.
examples.translation: Maaari itong may mga opsyonal na parameter.
examples.suggested: Opsyonal na magkaroon ito ng mga parameter.
examples.why: "Maaari itong may ..." is ungrammatical — "maaari" needs a verb ("magkaroon"), not "may". Reads as MT output rather than something a Tagalog technical writer would produce.

examples.source: The template circuit is structurally equivalent to the original circuit.
examples.translation: Ang template circuit ay structurally katumbas ng orihinal na circuit.
examples.suggested: Ang template circuit ay katumbas sa istruktura ng orihinal na circuit.
examples.why: The bare English adverb "structurally" is dropped into a Tagalog clause where an adverbial phrase is required; a calque a native editor would rewrite.

examples.source: Typically, each item consists of a circuit, a set of parameter values, and possibly a samplex ...
examples.translation: Karaniwang, ang bawat item ay binubuo ng isang circuit, isang set ng mga halaga ng parameter, at posibleng isang `samplex` ...
examples.suggested: Karaniwan, ang bawat item ay binubuo ng isang circuit, ...
examples.why: As a sentence-initial adverb set off by a comma the form is "Karaniwan"; the linker -ng attaches only when it directly modifies a following word. Small grammatical polish, no meaning impact.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful end-to-end — the negations and conditions that matter all survive: the "huwag ihanda at mag-sample mula sa eksaktong ground state" emphasis in §3.1, the Case-2 conclusion that excluding target basis states "bahagi man o buo" gives a different ground state, and the whole §5 VQE/SQD table (upper bound, 2951 → 1187 groupings, 10^5-10^7 shots) are all correct. What a native editor would fix is mechanical: line 31 has an ungrammatical double-"ang" calque, "nagiging mahal ang computationally ang pamamaraan" (should be "nagiging magastos sa kompyutasyon ang pamamaraan"); line 400 uses the adjectival "eksaktong" twice with no following noun ("ay eksaktong, ibig sabihin ang mga nakalkulang eigenvalue ay eksaktong sa subspace na iyon") where plain "eksakto" is required; line 408 has the typo "kalamanan" for "kalamangan". Separately, "span" is rendered three ways within the file — "sakop ng" (lines 62, 118, 124, 169, 353), "binuo ng" (216), and a coined salok-verb "sasalukin/masalukin/susalukin" (268, 275, 312) — where "sakop/saklaw" alone would read as written by a Tagalog-speaking physicist; the salok forms are the odd ones out. Register is consistently casual with no po/opo slips, and domain terms (Hamiltonian, eigenvalue, subspace, ansatz, shots, variational) are kept in English as the field does.

examples.source: However, the approach becomes computationally expensive (even impossible) as the matrix gets larger.
examples.translation: Gayunpaman, nagiging mahal ang computationally ang pamamaraan (maging imposible) habang lumalaki ang matrix.
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, nagiging magastos sa kompyutasyon ang pamamaraan (maging imposible pa nga) habang lumalaki ang matrix.
examples.why: Ungrammatical double-'ang' with a bare English adverb dropped in mid-clause; no native technical writer would produce this construction. Meaning is still recoverable, so minor.

examples.source: the energy estimations using diagonalization process are exact, meaning the computed eigenvalues are exact in that subspace
examples.translation: ang mga energy estimation gamit ang diagonalization process ay eksaktong, ibig sabihin ang mga nakalkulang eigenvalue ay eksaktong sa subspace na iyon
examples.suggested: ...ay eksakto, ibig sabihin ang mga nakalkulang eigenvalue ay eksakto sa subspace na iyon
examples.why: The linker -ng on 'eksakto' is left dangling with no noun after it, twice in one sentence. Reads as unproofed MT output rather than edited prose.

examples.source: The sampled basis states (bitstrings) will span the subspace / to span the subspace
examples.translation: ay sasalukin ang subspace / upang masalukin ang subspace / kung susalukin natin ang subspace — versus 'ang ground state ng matrix ay sakop ng dalawang computational basis states'
examples.suggested: Use the sakop/saklaw family throughout: 'ang mga na-sample na basis state ang sasaklaw sa subspace', 'upang masaklaw ang subspace', 'kung sasaklawin natin ang subspace'.
examples.why: 'Span' is split within the file between 'sakop', 'binuo ng', and a coined verb from 'salok' (to scoop/draw water), which is not the mathematical sense. The concept stays identifiable, so this is inconsistency, not a false concept.

examples.source: **Many shots per circuit for tighter variance**.
examples.translation: **Maraming shots bawat circuit para sa mas mataas na katumpakan**.
examples.suggested: **Maraming shots bawat circuit para sa mas masikip na variance**.
examples.why: 'Tighter variance' is flattened to 'higher accuracy', dropping the variance framing that the very next sentence builds on ('may kalakip na variance na nakasalalay sa inverse ng sqrt(shots)'). Not misleading, but the pedagogical thread is weakened.

examples.source: SQD has several advantages over VQE such as lower measurement overhead
examples.translation: Ang SQD ay may ilang kalamanan sa VQE tulad ng mas mababang measurement overhead
examples.suggested: Ang SQD ay may ilang kalamangan kaysa sa VQE tulad ng mas mababang measurement overhead
examples.why: 'kalamanan' is a typo for 'kalamangan'; also 'sa VQE' reads as 'in VQE' rather than 'over VQE' — 'kaysa sa VQE' is the comparative the English intends.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the technical content tracks the English faithfully (optimization_level 0 = "pinakamababa" doing "pinakamaliit na kinakailangan", 3 = "pinakamataas", the two-qubit gate/decoherence rationale, dynamical decoupling on "mga idle na qubit", and the Hellinger caveat "mas mataas ay mas mabuti, at ang 1 ay perpektong fidelity" are all intact). What a native technical editor would change is a handful of calques and one wrong verb: "itago ang mga resulta sa `result`" uses itago (= to hide) where the source says "store" — iimbak/i-save is the right word; "at the expense of" becomes the literal "sa kapinsalaan ng" (kapalit ng is the idiom); "should perform much better" becomes the stiff "dapat na mas mahusay na magsagawa", which also drops the intensifier "much"; and "transpile against custom backends" is rendered "mag-transpile laban sa mga custom na backend", where laban sa reads as "versus" rather than "targeting". Also note "pareho" carries both senses in the file — "ang parehong setting" (the same setting) vs "para sa parehong halaga ng optimization_level" (both values) — context disambiguates, but "dalawang halaga" would be safer. Sequential "Finally" is rendered "Sa wakas" (at last, with relief) instead of "Panghuli".

examples.source: run these circuits using the Sampler primitive and store the results to `result`
examples.translation: patakbuhin ang mga circuit na ito gamit ang Sampler primitive at itago ang mga resulta sa `result`
examples.suggested: ... at iimbak (o i-save) ang mga resulta sa `result`
examples.why: itago means "to hide/conceal" in Tagalog, not "to store". Harmless in context because the code is right beside it, but it is the wrong verb for assignment/storage.

examples.source: the circuit transpiled with `optimization_level=3` should perform much better
examples.translation: ang circuit na na-transpile gamit ang `optimization_level=3` ay dapat na mas mahusay na magsagawa
examples.suggested: ... ay dapat na mas mahusay ang performance / dapat mas maganda ang resulta nito
examples.why: "magsagawa" calques English "perform" in the sense of "carry out", producing a construction no Tagalog technical writer would use; the intensifier "much" is also dropped.

examples.source: often at the expense of longer classical processing time
examples.translation: kadalasan sa kapinsalaan ng mas matagal na classical processing time
examples.suggested: kadalasan ay kapalit ng mas matagal na classical processing time
examples.why: "sa kapinsalaan ng" is a literal rendering of "at the expense of" and means "to the injury/damage of"; the trade-off sense is carried by "kapalit ng".

examples.source: Create and transpile against custom backends
examples.translation: Lumikha at mag-transpile laban sa mga custom na backend
examples.suggested: Lumikha at mag-transpile para sa mga custom na backend
examples.why: "laban sa" reads as "against/versus" (adversarial), while the English "against" here means "targeting"; the link label loses its meaning.

examples.source: Finally, plot the results from the device runs against the ideal distribution.
examples.translation: Sa wakas, i-plot ang mga resulta mula sa mga pagpapatakbo ng device laban sa ideal na distribusyon.
examples.suggested: Panghuli, i-plot ang mga resulta ...
examples.why: "Sa wakas" carries the sense of "at long last" (relief); the neutral step-sequence marker in instructional Tagalog is "Panghuli".

editor_note: The lesson's opening definition inverts the cost function's purpose: "for the optimizer to minimize (or maximize)" becomes "para mapakinabangan (o mapinalaki) ng optimizer" — and the same file uses "mapakinabangan" to render *maximize* elsewhere ("upang mapakinabangan ang bilang ng mga gilid" for max-cut, line 467), so the learner is told at the outset that the optimizer maximizes (or enlarges) the cost function, when the whole lesson is built on minimization (later correctly rendered as "i-minimize" at lines 353/529). "mapinalaki" is also a malformed verb (should be "mapalaki"). Second drift: the qubit-ordering caveat "(recall that the 0th qubit is farthest right)" becomes "(alalahanin na ang 0th qubit ay pinakamalayo sa kanan)", which in Tagalog reads as *farthest from the right* (i.e. leftmost) — exactly the reverse of the convention needed to read IIZZ + IZIZ + …. Beyond these, "expectation value" is split three ways within the file ("inaasahang halaga" in the Primitives sections, then bare "expectation value" from line 353 on, plus "expected value" at line 502), several DefinitionTooltip definitions are left wholly in English (black-box quantum oracle at 366, overhead at 678, bias at 796) while the earlier ones at 29/64 were translated, and a handful of calques read as MT ("nagmumula ang `Estimator` ng bagong circuit" for "derives a new circuit", "sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng katotohanan na" for "by virtue of noting that", "Sa kahirapan" for "With great difficulty").

examples.source: This is a problem-specific function that defines the problem's goal for the optimizer to minimize (or maximize)
examples.translation: Ito ay isang function na naka-depende sa problema na nagtatakda ng layunin ng problema para mapakinabangan (o mapinalaki) ng optimizer
examples.suggested: ...na nagtatakda ng layunin ng problema na i-minimize (o i-maximize) ng optimizer
examples.why: 'mapakinabangan' is the file's own rendering of *maximize* (line 467, max-cut). Minimization — the entire premise of the lesson and of every later formula (min_θ ⟨ψ|H|ψ⟩) — is inverted to maximization in the defining sentence, and 'mapinalaki' (a malformed 'mapalaki', to enlarge) does not recover the contrast.

examples.source: (recall that the 0th qubit is farthest right)
examples.translation: (alalahanin na ang 0th qubit ay pinakamalayo sa kanan)
examples.suggested: (alalahanin na ang 0th qubit ang nasa pinakakanan)
examples.why: 'malayo sa kanan' means far FROM the right; the natural reading is 'farthest from the right' = leftmost, reversing the bit-ordering convention the learner needs to parse IIZZ, IZIZ, IZZI, ZIIZ, ZZII correctly.

examples.source: expectation value / expected value
examples.translation: 'inaasahang halaga' (lines 56, 62, 83, 90) → 'expectation value' (353, 359, 736, 928) → 'expected value' (502)
examples.suggested: Pick one — e.g. keep 'expectation value' throughout, as the later half does
examples.why: The single most-used quantity in the lesson is rendered three ways within one file; the concept stays identifiable, but a reader tracking it across the Estimator section and the Cost functions section sees three labels for one thing.

examples.source: `Estimator` derives a new circuit $V_k|\psi\rangle$ for each observable
examples.translation: nagmumula ang `Estimator` ng bagong circuit na $V_k|\psi\rangle$ para sa bawat observable
examples.suggested: bumubuo ang `Estimator` ng bagong circuit na $V_k|\psi\rangle$ para sa bawat observable
examples.why: 'nagmumula' is intransitive (to originate from) and cannot take an object; no native technical writer would write 'nagmumula ang Estimator ng circuit'. Same class of slip at line 117 ('sa pamamagitan ng paggawa ng katotohanan na' for 'by virtue of noting that') and line 928 ('Sa kahirapan' for 'With great difficulty').

examples.source: DefinitionTooltip definition="A hypothetical device or software component…" / "Extra costs introduced by new techniques…" / "A systematic drift in the measured quantities…"
examples.translation: left verbatim in English, while the equivalent tooltips at lines 29 and 64 are fully translated
examples.suggested: Translate these three definition strings to match the treatment of the 'primitives' and 'Pauli operators' tooltips
examples.why: Inconsistent coverage inside one page: a Tagalog reader gets a translated gloss for 'primitive' and 'Pauli operator' but an English-only gloss for 'black-box quantum oracle', 'overhead' and 'bias' — the three glosses that matter most in the measurement-strategy section.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere — every list item, the negation in "Hindi nangangailangan ng authentication ang Qiskit MCP Server at Qiskit Docs MCP Server," and the version requirement "Python 3.10 o mas bago (inirerekomenda ang 3.11+)" all match the English, and the register stays casual (no po/opo). What an editor would change is prose-level: the Qiskit Docs MCP Server paragraph has a genuine marker error, "Nagbibigay ng access ng mga AI assistant sa kumpletong ekosistema…" (should be "Nagbibigay sa mga AI assistant ng access sa…"), and "Pinapahintulutan" ("permits") is used five times in a row as a mechanical stand-in for both "enables" and "allows," which reads as calqued repetition where a native writer would alternate with "Nagbibigay-daan sa." Smaller slips: "directly" is dropped from "Pagsagot sa mga tanong sa quantum computing mula sa mga mapagkakatiwalaang pinagkukunan," and "maaaring magmukha tulad nito" is stiff for "might look like this" (natural: "maaaring ganito ang hitsura"). The Qiskit domain term "job" is rendered as "trabaho" — over-translated but at least consistent across both occurrences.

examples.source: Provides AI assistants with access to the complete Qiskit documentation ecosystem
examples.translation: Nagbibigay ng access ng mga AI assistant sa kumpletong ekosistema ng dokumentasyon ng Qiskit
examples.suggested: Nagbibigay sa mga AI assistant ng access sa kumpletong ekosistema ng dokumentasyon ng Qiskit
examples.why: The case markers are swapped: 'ng mga AI assistant' makes the assistants the thing being given rather than the recipient. A native technical writer would use 'sa mga AI assistant ng access sa…'.

examples.source: enables / allow (AI assistants to …)
examples.translation: Pinapahintulutan ng … ang mga AI assistant na …
examples.suggested: Nagbibigay-daan sa mga AI assistant na … (vary with 'Tinutulungan nito ang…')
examples.why: 'Pinapahintulutan' means 'permits/grants permission', which is a narrower sense than 'enables', and it is repeated identically six times. The mechanical repetition reads as machine translation rather than authored Tagalog technical prose.

examples.source: Answering quantum computing questions directly from reliable sources
examples.translation: Pagsagot sa mga tanong sa quantum computing mula sa mga mapagkakatiwalaang pinagkukunan
examples.suggested: Pagsagot sa mga tanong sa quantum computing nang direkta mula sa mga mapagkakatiwalaang pinagkukunan
examples.why: The qualifier 'directly' is dropped. It carries the selling point (answers sourced straight from authoritative docs rather than model recall), so the emphasis is flattened, though the sentence is not misleading.

examples.source: tracking job status / submit jobs
examples.translation: pagsubaybay ng katayuan ng trabaho / magsumite ng mga trabaho
examples.suggested: pagsubaybay sa status ng job / magsumite ng mga job
examples.why: In Qiskit Runtime, 'job' is a named object (Job, job ID, job status) that the field keeps in English; 'trabaho' reads as generic 'work' and disconnects the reader from the API surface. Consistent within the file, so recognizable — but imperfect.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — I checked the whole Pauli-decomposition argument, the syndrome/product-state passage ("Mahalaga, ito ay isang product state… Wala nang ugnayan sa sistema sa kanan"), the "single-qubit operation can't change the logical state" paragraph, and the Kraus/Generalization sections in the last 40%; no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims, and the Pauli/syndrome/channel terminology is consistent. What a native technical editor would change is the discourse-marker layer, which is calqued rather than written: "Pagkatapos ng lahat" for "After all" (line ~21, means "after everything", not the concessive marker), "napakagaling para maging totoo" for "too good to be true" (line ~113; idiom is "masyadong maganda para maging totoo"), "Sa wakas" for enumerative "Finally" (line ~119; should be "Panghuli"), "Sa katumpakan" for "To be precise" (line ~120), and a bare "Konsepto," for "Conceptually speaking" (line ~163), which is ungrammatical as an adverbial and needs "Sa konsepto". Smaller slips: "hindi koruptong encoding" (line ~104) uses the moral/political sense of corrupt where "hindi nasirang" is meant; "Mahahanap natin na" (line ~10) is a literal "we'll find" where "Makikita natin" is idiomatic; "kinukuha… ang error syndrome" (line ~145) softens "compute"; and two typos, "maari" (line ~22) and "susukathin" (line ~78). "Measurement" also drifts between kept-English ("measurement outcome", "standard basis measurements") and "sukat"/"pag-sukat" — recognizable, but not one convention. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: After all, there are infinitely many possible errors like this
examples.translation: Pagkatapos ng lahat, walang katapusang bilang ng posibleng ganitong mga error
examples.suggested: Kung tutuusin, walang katapusang bilang ng posibleng ganitong mga error
examples.why: "Pagkatapos ng lahat" is a word-for-word calque; in Tagalog it means "after everything/at the end", not the concessive discourse marker "after all". A native technical writer would use "Kung tutuusin" or "Sa katunayan".

examples.source: At first glance it may seem too good to be true
examples.translation: Sa unang tingin, maaaring mukhang napakagaling para maging totoo
examples.suggested: Sa unang tingin, maaaring mukhang masyadong maganda para maging totoo
examples.why: "napakagaling" means "extremely skilled/impressive", which misfires on the idiom; the settled Tagalog rendering of "too good to be true" is "masyadong maganda para maging totoo".

examples.source: Conceptually speaking, the idea is identical to the unitary case.
examples.translation: Konsepto, ang ideya ay kapareho ng unitary na kaso.
examples.suggested: Sa konsepto, ang ideya ay kapareho ng unitary na kaso.
examples.why: A bare noun "Konsepto," cannot function as a sentence adverbial in Tagalog; it reads as a truncated MT output. "Sa konsepto" (or "Sa antas ng konsepto") is the natural form.

examples.source: we have our original, uncorrupted encoding as the right-hand tensor factor
examples.translation: mayroon tayong orihinal, hindi koruptong encoding bilang right-hand tensor factor
examples.suggested: mayroon tayong orihinal, hindi nasirang encoding bilang right-hand tensor factor
examples.why: "korupto" in Tagalog carries the moral/political sense (bribery, dishonesty); for data or state corruption the idiomatic word is "nasira"/"hindi nasira". Recognizable but wrong sense of the word.

examples.source: measurements / measurement outcomes / we'll measure
examples.translation: ang mga sukat na nagbibigay sa atin ng syndrome bits … mga measurement outcome … 8 qubits na susukathin natin … nasukat na syndrome
examples.suggested: Pick one convention (e.g. keep "measurement" in English throughout, with the verb "sukatin"), and fix the typo "susukathin" → "susukatin".
examples.why: "measurement" is rendered three ways within the file — kept English, nominalized as "sukat" (which normally means "size"), and verbal "sukatin" — plus a typo. Concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip, not a meaning error.

editor_note: No hallucinated content and no inverted conditions or swapped quantities — the five numbered TEM benefits, the IC-POVM description, and the noiseless-circuit caveat (`0.18409094298943401`) all survive intact — so this is not a FAIL. What a native technical editor would fix: the noise-learning sentence uses the wrong voice, "Ang ingay na nakaka-apekto sa mga layer ay natututo sa pamamagitan ng Qiskit Runtime" reads as "the noise learns" instead of "is learned" (natututunan/inaaral), while the very next paragraph correctly says "ang natutunan na ingay". "Steps to reproduce the issue" became "Mga hakbang upang maparami ang isyu" — maparami means "to multiply/increase in number", not to reproduce a bug (dapat: "upang maulit ang isyu"). Mathematical "inverse" is rendered as "kabaligtaran" (opposite) rather than the inverse of the noise channel, and "expectation/expected value" is kept as English "expected value" throughout the Overview but switches to "inaasahang halaga" in the final admonition; plus MT-flavored spots like "Maaari mong ibalik ang mga resulta" ("return" as give-back) and "pagtatayo ng isang tensor network" (pagtatayo = erecting a building).

examples.source: The noise affecting the layers is learned through Qiskit Runtime using a sparse Pauli-Lindblad noise model
examples.translation: Ang ingay na nakaka-apekto sa mga layer ay natututo sa pamamagitan ng Qiskit Runtime gamit ang isang sparse Pauli-Lindblad noise model
examples.suggested: Ang ingay na nakakaapekto sa mga layer ay natututunan sa pamamagitan ng Qiskit Runtime gamit ang isang sparse Pauli-Lindblad noise model
examples.why: Active 'natututo' makes the noise the learner; the English has Qiskit Runtime learning the noise. The file itself uses the correct passive form one paragraph later ('ang natutunan na ingay'), so the voice slip is internally inconsistent too.

examples.source: Steps to reproduce the issue
examples.translation: Mga hakbang upang maparami ang isyu
examples.suggested: Mga hakbang upang maulit (o ma-reproduce) ang isyu
examples.why: 'Maparami' means to increase in number / multiply. As written the support checklist asks the user for steps to make the problem more numerous rather than steps to recreate it.

examples.source: constructing a tensor network representing the inverse of the global noise channel
examples.translation: pagtatayo ng isang tensor network na kumakatawan sa kabaligtaran ng pandaigdigang noise channel
examples.suggested: pagbuo ng isang tensor network na kumakatawan sa inverse ng global noise channel
examples.why: 'Kabaligtaran' is everyday 'opposite', not the mathematical inverse of a channel — the operation TEM actually applies. 'Pagtatayo' (erecting/constructing a structure) is also the wrong collocation for building a tensor network; 'pagbuo' is the natural choice.

examples.source: expectation values of observables / The expected value for the noiseless circuit
examples.translation: mga expected value ng mga observable ... / Ang inaasahang halaga para sa noiseless circuit ...
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (e.g. keep 'expectation value' or use 'inaasahang halaga') and use it in both places
examples.why: The same concept is kept in English in the Overview/Description and translated in the closing admonition, so the reader cannot tell that the `0.184...` figure is the same quantity the whole page has been estimating.

examples.source: You can return the results as:
examples.translation: Maaari mong ibalik ang mga resulta tulad nito:
examples.suggested: Makukuha mo ang mga resulta tulad nito:
examples.why: 'Ibalik' is 'give back / send back' — a literal calque of 'return'. In the code sense the results are retrieved, not handed back, so a Tagalog engineer would write 'makuha/makukuha'.

examples.source: TEM significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of digital quantum simulations
examples.translation: Ang TEM ay malaki ang naiaambag sa katumpakan at pagiging maaasahan ng mga digital quantum simulation
examples.suggested: Malaki ang ipinagpapabuti ng TEM sa katumpakan at pagiging maaasahan ng mga digital quantum simulation
examples.why: 'Naiaambag' (contributes to) is weaker than 'improves' — it says TEM adds to accuracy rather than raising it, softening the benefit claim in a bullet whose whole point is the size of the improvement.

examples.source: Once the circuits are submitted to the function, they are transpiled and optimized
examples.translation: Kapag naisumite na ang mga circuit sa function, sila ay ita-transpile at io-optimize
examples.suggested: Kapag naisumite na ang mga circuit sa function, ang mga ito ay ita-transpile at io-optimize
examples.why: 'Sila' is the animate/personal plural pronoun; using it for circuits is a direct calque of English 'they' and reads as machine output to a native technical writer.

editor_note: No misleading content: every numeric claim, criterion and pass/fail verdict tracks the English (fidelity > 0.5, 40,000 shots, "tumaas ang tree depth mula 5 hanggang 6, bumaba ang two-qubit depth mula 9 hanggang 8", the three "hindi natutugunan ang pamantayan" outcomes), register is consistently casual with no po/opo, and core terms (qubit, circuit, backend, fidelity, transpile, Sampler/Estimator, shots) are kept in English and used consistently. The defects are word-choice, not meaning: "to work with a GHZ state on more qubits" became "para makipagtulungan sa isang GHZ state" — makipagtulungan means to collaborate/cooperate with a person, which no Filipino engineer would write of a quantum state ("gumamit ng" / "gumawa sa" is the natural verb). "These approaches build on strategies you already know" became "nadagdag sa mga estratehiya na alam mo na" ("were added to"), losing the "nakabatay sa" (built upon) relation, and "Surprisingly" became "Kahanga-hanga" (impressive/admirable) instead of "Nakakagulat", flattening the counterintuitive point the sentence is teaching. Two small intensifier/consistency slips also: "much lower than that in the chain structure" lost its "much" ("mas mababa na" only), and "set the shots number as 40,000" is rendered "bilang 40,000" in §1.2 but the better "sa 40,000" in §5.

examples.source: But to work with a GHZ state on more qubits, you will clearly need to think about optimizing the circuit.
examples.translation: Ngunit para makipagtulungan sa isang GHZ state na may mas maraming qubit, kailangan mong mag-isip tungkol sa pag-optimize ng circuit.
examples.suggested: Ngunit para makagawa ng GHZ state na may mas maraming qubit, malinaw na kailangan mong isipin ang pag-optimize ng circuit.
examples.why: makipagtulungan = to collaborate/cooperate (with a person); using it of a quantum state is a literal calque of "work with" that a native technical writer would never produce. The dropped "clearly" (malinaw na) also softens the emphasis slightly.

examples.source: These approaches build on strategies you already know from previous lessons.
examples.translation: Ang mga diskarteng ito ay nadagdag sa mga estratehiya na alam mo na mula sa mga nakaraang aralin.
examples.suggested: Ang mga diskarteng ito ay nakabatay sa mga estratehiyang alam mo na mula sa mga nakaraang aralin.
examples.why: "nadagdag sa" says the approaches were *added to* the earlier strategies, reversing the pedagogical relation — the English says they are *built on* prior knowledge. Not misleading about the physics, but it weakens the continuity cue for the learner. Same sentence also mixes diskarte/estratehiya for one concept.

examples.source: Surprisingly, while the tree depth increased from 5 to 6, the two-qubit depth decreased from 9 to 8!
examples.translation: Kahanga-hanga, kahit na tumaas ang tree depth mula 5 hanggang 6, bumaba ang two-qubit depth mula 9 hanggang 8!
examples.suggested: Nakakagulat, kahit tumaas ang tree depth mula 5 tungo sa 6, bumaba ang two-qubit depth mula 9 tungo sa 8!
examples.why: Kahanga-hanga means impressive/admirable, not surprising. The whole point of the sentence is that the result is counterintuitive (deeper tree, shallower two-qubit depth); rendering it as praise flattens the teaching beat. Numbers themselves are faithful to the source.

examples.source: The depth of the circuit has now become much lower than that in the chain structure.
examples.translation: Ang depth ng circuit ay naging mas mababa na kaysa sa chain structure.
examples.suggested: Mas mababa na ngayon nang malaki ang depth ng circuit kaysa sa chain structure.
examples.why: "much" is dropped, so the tree-vs-chain improvement (22/6 vs 27/8) reads as a marginal gain rather than the substantial one the English asserts; the passive "ay naging" construction is also stiffer than a native writer's fronted predicate.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the retirement table, the CRN admonition (the "lamang" in "mula sa instansyang iyon lamang ang available" correctly carries the English "only", and the negated conditional "Kung hindi tinukoy ang isang instansya" is intact), and the deprecated-provider note ("hindi na available") all match the source, and the register stays informal throughout. What a native technical editor would still change: (a) a spelling error, "nang hindi sinasasakripisyo ang performance" in the Eagle bullet — should be "sinasakripisyo"; (b) tense slippage on the retired processor families, which the English keeps uniformly in the past — "nag-aalok" (Falcon) and "gumagamit" (Eagle) are imperfective/present and sit oddly beside the correctly past "nagsilbi ring" in the very same Falcon sentence; (c) "instansya" for *instance*, which in ordinary Tagalog reads as a legal/court instance — the field normally keeps "instance"; (d) the Egret bullet's "mas mabilis at mas mataas na fidelity ng two-qubit gate" collapses the two parallel adjectives of "faster and higher-fidelity two-qubit gates" into a single awkward possessive chain. None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the API.

examples.source: allowing high-density I/O without sacrificing performance.
examples.translation: na nagbibigay-daan sa high-density I/O nang hindi sinasasakripisyo ang performance.
examples.suggested: na nagbibigay-daan sa high-density I/O nang hindi isinasakripisyo ang performance.
examples.why: Typo: "sinasasakripisyo" has a doubled syllable; the correct form is "isinasakripisyo"/"sinasakripisyo".

examples.source: The Falcon family of devices offered a valuable platform for medium-scale circuits, and also served as a valuable platform...
examples.translation: Ang pamilyang Falcon ng mga device ay nag-aalok ng mahalagang plataporma para sa mga medium-scale na Circuit, at nagsilbi ring mahalagang plataporma...
examples.suggested: Ang pamilyang Falcon ng mga device ay nag-alok ng mahalagang plataporma para sa mga medium-scale na Circuit, at nagsilbi ring...
examples.why: The English is uniformly past tense because these processors are retired; "nag-aalok" is imperfective and clashes with the past-tense "nagsilbi" in the same sentence. Same slip in the Eagle bullet: "gumagamit" for "incorporated" (better: "gumamit").

examples.source: If an instance is not specified, all backends and jobs across all instances in your account are available.
examples.translation: Kung hindi tinukoy ang isang instansya, lahat ng backend at job sa lahat ng instansya sa iyong account ay available.
examples.suggested: Kung walang tinukoy na instance, available ang lahat ng backend at job sa lahat ng instance sa iyong account.
examples.why: "instansya" reads in everyday Tagalog as a legal/court instance; the IBM Quantum platform term is normally kept as "instance", consistent with "backend", "job", and "account" being kept in this same sentence.

examples.source: resulting in faster and higher-fidelity two-qubit gates.
examples.translation: na nagresulta sa mas mabilis at mas mataas na fidelity ng two-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: na nagresulta sa mas mabilis at mas mataas ang fidelity na mga two-qubit gate.
examples.why: The two parallel modifiers of "gates" get collapsed into one possessive chain, so "mas mabilis" ends up modifying "fidelity" rather than the gates; meaning is still recoverable but the phrasing is calqued.
