editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every load-bearing number and claim survives (90 training / 30 test points, 128 rows × 14 features + 15th label, 42 features, 2^10 = 1024, 0.90^10 ≈ 35%, (1-p)^N, depth 60 vs 77 across 20 transpilations, "two-qubit depth >100 even before transpilation is a non-starter"), and no condition is inverted or caveat dropped. What a native editor would change is lexical: "relative measurement probabilities" is rendered "mga kamag-anak na posibilidad ng pagsukat" — "kamag-anak" is a family relative, an MT artifact no Tagalog engineer would write; "the shallowest circuit" becomes "ang pinakamabanayad na circuit" ("gentlest/mildest") where the file elsewhere correctly says "pinakamababang-depth na circuit"; and "probability" is split within the file between "posibilidad" (15×, the looser "possibility") and the correct technical "probabilidad" (2×, only in the final "Pag-scale at mga gawain sa hinaharap" section). Also several typos/slips: "pagmamagang ito" (for pagmamapang), "ang simmetry ng kernel matrix", "ang pinakamalim na circuit", "masukat nating ang |0⟩", "maaaring masukatan". Register is correctly casual (no po/opo), and the added line under "Suriin ang iyong pag-unawa" ("i-click ang mga tatsulok…") is a repo-wide accordion→details adaptation, not a defect.

examples.source: the kernel is estimated using measurements on that circuit and the relative measurement probabilities
examples.translation: tinatantiya ang kernel gamit ang mga sukat sa circuit na iyon at ang mga kamag-anak na posibilidad ng pagsukat
examples.suggested: …at ang mga kaugnay na probabilidad ng pagsukat
examples.why: "kamag-anak" is a family relative — a literal MT rendering of "relative" that is nonsense in a measurement-statistics context; "kaugnay/relatibo" is the technical sense.

examples.source: It is often useful to transpile a few times and take the shallowest circuit.
examples.translation: Kadalasang kapaki-pakinabang na mag-transpile ng ilang beses at gamitin ang pinakamabanayad na circuit.
examples.suggested: …at gamitin ang pinakamababaw (pinakamababa ang depth) na circuit.
examples.why: "mabanayad" means gentle/mild, not shallow; the selection criterion (minimum depth) is stated correctly later as "pinakamababang-depth na circuit" (Review section), so the file also contradicts itself.

examples.source: probability / probability distribution
examples.translation: posibilidad, distribusyon ng posibilidad (15×) vs probabilidad (2×, only in the final section)
examples.suggested: probabilidad / distribusyon ng probabilidad throughout
examples.why: "posibilidad" is "possibility", not the statistical term; the file switches to the correct "probabilidad" only in the last section, so one concept carries two names.

examples.source: many such inner products between mapped data vectors … denote the mapped states
examples.translation: sa pagitan ng mga nakaprosesong data vector … tukuyin ang mga nakaprosesong estado
examples.suggested: mga na-map (naimapang) data vector … ang mga na-map na estado
examples.why: "nakaproseso" = "processed" flattens the specific feature-map operation the whole lesson is built on, while the same paragraph uses "pagmamapa" for the identical English verb.

examples.source: symmetry of a kernel matrix / the deepest circuit obtained / we measure the |0⟩ as accurately as possible
examples.translation: ang simmetry ng kernel matrix / ang pinakamalim na circuit na nakuha / masukat nating ang $|0\rangle$
examples.suggested: ang simetriya ng kernel matrix / ang pinakamalalim na circuit / masukat natin ang $|0\rangle$
examples.why: Three typo-level slips a native technical editor would fix on sight: a half-anglicized "simmetry", a truncated superlative "pinakamalim", and a stray enclitic "nating ang".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the TTL/timeout logic, the session-status list, and the close-vs-cancel distinction ("Titigil ang session sa pagtanggap ng mga bagong job ngunit patuloy na magpapatakbo ng mga naka-queue na job nang may priyoridad") all carry the English conditions intact, with no inverted negation, swapped quantity, or dropped caveat, and register stays casual (no po/opo). What a native editor would fix is smaller: a real typo in the VQE section, "bawisa ay gumagamit ng ibang klasikal na optimizer" (should be "bawat isa"); "respectively" rendered as "ayon sa pagkakataon" instead of the standard "ayon sa pagkakabanggit"; "minimize a cost function" flattened to "mabawasan ang isang cost function" ("reduce"), which loses the optimization sense a learner needs; and "differentiate jobs" rendered as "mapaghiwalay" ("separate") where "makilala/matukoy ang pagkakaiba" is what tags actually do. None of these teaches a false concept — they are wording slips, not drift.

examples.source: The following example shows how you can run two VQE algorithms, each using a different classical optimizer, simultaneously inside a single session.
examples.translation: Ipinapakita ng sumusunod na halimbawa kung paano mo maaaring patakbuhin ang dalawang VQE algorithm, bawisa ay gumagamit ng ibang klasikal na optimizer, nang sabay-sabay sa loob ng iisang session.
examples.suggested: ...dalawang VQE algorithm, na ang bawat isa ay gumagamit ng ibang klasikal na optimizer, ...
examples.why: "bawisa" is a typo for "bawat isa"; as written it is not a Tagalog word and the relative clause loses its anchor. Meaning is still recoverable, so minor.

examples.source: ...look for the `max_time` or `interactive_timeout` value, respectively.
examples.translation: ...hanapin ang value ng `max_time` o `interactive_timeout`, ayon sa pagkakataon.
examples.suggested: ...hanapin ang value ng `max_time` o `interactive_timeout`, ayon sa pagkakabanggit.
examples.why: "ayon sa pagkakataon" means "as the occasion arises", not "respectively"; the standard Tagalog rendering is "ayon sa pagkakabanggit". The pairing of the two values to the two TTLs is what the sentence is doing, so the idiom matters.

examples.source: Run an iterative workload that uses the classical SciPy optimizer to minimize a cost function.
examples.translation: Magpatakbo ng iterative workload na gumagamit ng klasikal na SciPy optimizer para mabawasan ang isang cost function.
examples.suggested: ...para i-minimize ang isang cost function.
examples.why: "mabawasan" reads as "to reduce/lessen" rather than the optimization term "minimize"; a learner meeting VQE for the first time loses the sense that the optimizer is driving the cost to its minimum, not just making it smaller.

examples.source: Job tags are also used to differentiate jobs from each workload.
examples.translation: Ginagamit din ang mga job tag para mapaghiwalay ang mga job mula sa bawat workload.
examples.suggested: Ginagamit din ang mga job tag para matukoy kung aling job ang galing sa bawat workload.
examples.why: "mapaghiwalay" means "to separate"; tags do not separate the jobs (they all run in one session) — they let you tell them apart. Small semantic shading, not misleading enough to fail.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the warning admonitions (including the source's own "na-export ng aming importer" quirk), the four required CustomInstruction fields, the `builtin=True` behavior, and the strict-mode caveat all survive intact, and register stays casual with no po/opo. The main defect is structural, not semantic: line 51 carries a stray, untranslated bullet "- Review the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic." dropped into the middle of the "Mag-import ng OpenQASM 2 program" section, duplicating a Next-steps item that has no counterpart in the source at that point. The rest are word-choice slips a native technical editor would fix: "gate statements it encounters" became "mga `gate` statement na nararamdaman nito" (feels/senses), "quality-of-life improvements" is calqued literally as "mga pagpapabuti sa kalidad ng buhay", "a callable Python object that evaluates the function" became "nagsusuri ng function" (examines/reviews rather than computes), and "You can extend the language with more functions" came out as the ungrammatical "palawakin ang wika ng mas maraming function". None of these would teach a learner a false concept.

examples.source: You can tell the importer to use specific `Gate` classes for the given `gate` statements it encounters.
examples.translation: Maaari mong sabihin sa importer na gumamit ng mga partikular na klase ng `Gate` para sa mga `gate` statement na nararamdaman nito.
examples.suggested: ...para sa mga `gate` statement na nakikita/natatagpuan nito.
examples.why: "nararamdaman" means "feels/senses" — a parser encounters statements, it does not feel them. No native technical writer would use it here.

examples.source: ...and several other quality-of-life improvements without emitting any errors.
examples.translation: ...at ilang iba pang mga pagpapabuti sa kalidad ng buhay nang hindi naglalabas ng anumang error.
examples.suggested: ...at ilang iba pang pagpapadali sa paggamit / mga pagpapabuti sa ginhawa ng paggamit...
examples.why: Literal calque: "kalidad ng buhay" is the human-welfare sense of quality of life, which is comic in a parser-leniency list.

examples.source: the specific example on working with the legacy exporter / a data attribute for working with OpenQASM 2 programs produced by legacy versions
examples.translation: ang partikular na halimbawa sa pakikipagtulungan sa legacy exporter / data attribute para sa pakikipagtulungan sa mga OpenQASM 2 program
examples.suggested: ...sa paggamit ng legacy exporter / ...para sa paggamit ng mga OpenQASM 2 program
examples.why: "pakikipagtulungan" is collaborating-with-a-person; you do not collaborate with an exporter or a program file. Stiff calque of "working with", repeated twice.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: the region caveat ("makikita at ma-access mo lamang ang mga instance na nilikha sa rehiyong naka-log in ka"), the trusted-vs-untrusted environment split, and the REST-API-instead-of-Qiskit condition all survive intact, and the informal register holds throughout (no po/opo). What a native technical editor would still fix is calqued English word order in three spots: "na nagpapahintulot ng IBM Quantum na access mula sa Qiskit" stacks an English noun-modifier onto "access" in a way Tagalog does not do; "Siguraduhing ang tamang account at rehiyon ay napili" uses an English-order passive where verb-initial "Siguraduhing napili ang tamang account at rehiyon" is the natural form; and "sa rehiyong naka-log in ka" drops the locative linker ("sa rehiyong kung saan ka naka-log in"). Terminology is consistent — instance, account switcher, header, API key, credential, QPU kept in English; "kapaligiran" used consistently for environment; "trabaho" consistently for jobs. These are fluency polish only, not misleading.

examples.source: a unique API token (also called a key) is assigned to each account, allowing for IBM Quantum access from Qiskit
examples.translation: isang natatanging API token (tinatawag din na key) ang itinalaga sa bawat account, na nagpapahintulot ng IBM Quantum na access mula sa Qiskit
examples.suggested: ...na nagbibigay-daan sa pag-access sa IBM Quantum mula sa Qiskit
examples.why: "IBM Quantum na access" is a direct calque of the English noun-modifier stack; Tagalog needs a nominalized verb (pag-access sa IBM Quantum). Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

examples.source: Make sure that the correct account and region are selected in the account switcher in the header
examples.translation: Siguraduhing ang tamang account at rehiyon ay napili sa account switcher sa header
examples.suggested: Siguraduhing napili ang tamang account at rehiyon sa account switcher sa header
examples.why: The "ang X ay Y" pattern mirrors English subject-verb order; native technical Tagalog is verb-initial here. Grammatical but stiff.

examples.source: you can only see and access the instances that were created in the region that you're logged in to
examples.translation: makikita at ma-access mo lamang ang mga instance na nilikha sa rehiyong naka-log in ka
examples.suggested: ...sa rehiyong kung saan ka naka-log in
examples.why: The locative relative clause is missing its linker, so "rehiyong naka-log in ka" reads clipped. The restriction itself (only instances in the logged-in region) is correctly preserved, including the "same API key works for either region" contrast.
